audit.why: 55.08% over 354 games — the best number in this slice — yet the chart hands Volibear five of the seven stages. That mismatch is deliberate and the prose explains it: Camille's edge here is tempo and map conversion off the Trinity Force spike rather than winning the stand-up brawl, which is exactly how a champion posts a high win rate in a lane she is not favoured to out-stat. The shape is defensible; I am not moving it.

Both ultimates are handled honestly at 6 — Camille isolates, but Stormbringer grants bonus health and an empowered all-in, so it is a skill fight rather than a free kill. Stormbringer is 160s at rank 1, the longest ultimate either champion has, and stating it turns 'respect this window' into something countable.

audit.whatIsWrong: Thundering Smash is described as a dash in five places — 'his Q dash closes the gap', 'the gaps between his Q dashes', 'its dash stuns you if he reaches you'. Sky Splitter (E) is absent from the entire matchup. Camille's R is written without its article.
audit.why: Riot flags Thundering Smash as an auto-attack reset with hard CC on a 300 range — it is a charge that grants movement speed and stuns with the next attack, not a dash. The distinction is the whole trade pattern: a dash arrives instantly and cannot be walked away from, a speed-up can be kited, and because it resets his attack the wind-up is the tell rather than the cast. _missing-interactions.json flags exactly this for the matchup. Meanwhile Sky Splitter is a 16s ranged ability that damages, slows and shields him — it is his poke and his answer to being kited, and a player who has never been told it exists will be surprised by it every game. Frenzied Maul is 5s, so his healing is effectively continuous in a brawl.
audit.corrected: Thundering Smash restated as a 12s speed-up into an auto-reset stun with the wind-up named as the tell; Sky Splitter named; Frenzied Maul's 5s given.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Trade in the gaps when his Q dash is down' and 'hold E for his Q dash' name his cooldown three times without giving it.
audit.why: Thundering Smash is 12s at rank 1 down to 10s, against Hookshot's 16s. His engage is back before hers is — so the instruction to hold E until he spends Q is right, but the reader needs to know they are giving up tempo to do it rather than trading evenly.
audit.corrected: 12s vs 16s written into whys[1] and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: Frenzied Maul's healing is cited three times as the thing that beats Camille in long fights and Grievous Wounds is never mentioned.
audit.why: _missing-interactions.json flags Frenzied Maul sustain and its on-hit scaling for this matchup. On a 5s cooldown with on-hit damage that scales with attack speed, it is both the reason armour alone reads his trades wrong and the reason anti-heal is the item that decides the late game the text keeps warning about.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds cue added to spikes[3].text and late.

edits.before: Volibear at Level 1-2 is a real threat — his W (Frenzied Maul) bite heals him and his Q dash closes the gap, so don't trade into a committed Q without your kit up. Your turn comes at 2-3: once Hookshot (E) and the empowered Q re-cast with its true-damage hit are online, you out-trade him cleanly. The key read is his Q (Thundering Smash) — its dash stuns you if he reaches you, so bait or dodge it, then wall-dash stun him and weave Q-Q while he has no dash to escape. Your passive shield will eat his first bite, so trigger it before you all-in.
edits.after: Volibear at Level 1-2 is a real threat — Frenzied Maul heals him every 5s and Thundering Smash speeds him into range, so don't trade into a committed charge without your kit up. Your turn comes at 2-3: once Hookshot and the true-damage Q re-cast are online you out-trade him cleanly. The key read is Thundering Smash: it is a 12s speed-up into an attack-reset stun, so the wind-up is the tell — walk out of it, then wall-dash him and weave Q-Q. Watch for Sky Splitter too, which slows you and shields him from range.

edits.before: Volibear is the scaler here — a full-build Volibear is a tanky brawler who heals through your W's percent damage with W (Frenzied Maul) and uses R (Stormbringer) to disable a tower and dive straight onto your carries. Your edge is tempo, not raw dueling, so use your first-item Trinity Force spike to take over side lanes and pick targets with your R isolation before his items come online. If the game drags to full builds he reclaims the 2+ items window, so win the map while your dive is the faster one.
edits.after: Volibear is the scaler — a full-build brawler who heals through your W's percent damage on a 5s Frenzied Maul and uses Stormbringer to disable a tower and dive your carries, so Grievous Wounds is what keeps your damage real. Your edge is tempo, not raw dueling: use the Trinity Force spike to take side lanes and pick targets with R isolation before his items land. If the game drags to full builds he reclaims 2+ items, so win the map while your dive is the faster one.

notes: Thundering Smash was written as a dash in five places. Riot's data flags it as an auto-attack reset with hard CC at 300 range — a charge that grants movement speed and stuns with the next attack. That changes the advice from 'dodge the dash' to 'the wind-up is the tell, walk out of it', which is the version _missing-interactions.json also generates for this pairing. Sky Splitter was absent from the matchup entirely despite being his only ranged tool and his shield. Grievous Wounds against a 5s Frenzied Maul was likewise missing even though three separate lines complain that his healing beats her in long fights.
